traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 162 Myrtaceae, 167 Combretaceae, 168 Melastomataceae, 288 Lythraceae and 289 Onagraceae, the bulk of APG's Myrtales: the sepals joined in a tube (a floral cup) round or on the ovary, the petals and stamens borne at its rim; leaves mostly opposite, alternate in some (Combretaceae, Onagraceae in part).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: APweb, Myrtales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): leaves of the order given as opposite; opposite pairs crossing is the decussate pattern. 'sometimes spiral' added because Combretaceae and Onagraceae include many alternate-leaved species. Weighting inferred from leaf_arrangement already stated for the order.

traits.leaf_division.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): leaves entire-margined and undivided across the families described (Combretaceae, Lythraceae, Onagraceae, Vochysiaceae all simple). Every family with candidates already states simple.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: APweb, Myrtales page, family notes (read 2026-10-16): most flowers regular; monosymmetry only in some genera (Cuphea, Lopezia) and in Vochysiaceae.

traits.zygomorphy.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): the zygomorphic members (Cuphea, Lopezia, Vochysiaceae) have neither pea-flower nor two-lipped nor orchid plans.

traits.flower_merosity.note: APweb, Myrtales page, order characterisation (read 2026-10-16): flowers often 4-merous; Onagraceae usually 4, Lythraceae typically 4, Combretaceae 4-5. Replaces the pentapetalae typical 5 for this order.

traits.ovary_position.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): ovary inferior at order level; Lythraceae more or less superior, Vochysiaceae either. 'usually' because Myrtaceae, Melastomataceae and Onagraceae (most species) are inferior.

traits.carpels.note: APweb, Myrtales page, family notes (read 2026-10-16): Combretaceae 2-5(-8), Lythraceae 2-6, Onagraceae usually 4, Vochysiaceae 3(-4).

traits.corolla_shape.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): petals free and borne on the hypanthium rim, spreading; no tubular corollas described. Shape inferred from free spreading petals.

traits.life_span.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): mostly trees and shrubs; herbs (some annual) only in Onagraceae and Lythraceae.

traits.rosette.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): leafy-stemmed woody plants and herbs; no rosette habit described for the order. Basal rosettes occur in some Oenothera (Onagraceae) only.

traits.sexual_system.note: APweb, Myrtales page (read 2026-10-16): flowers bisexual through most of the order; Combretaceae sometimes monoecious or dioecious (bracketed in source).
